existence_note: Lausanne is described as a historic city with medieval origins, ruled by the County of Savoy and the Bishop of Lausanne, indicating it existed long before 1850.
municipality_note: The present municipality of Lausanne exists in its current form since 2003, following the merger of several former municipalities within the Lausanne agglomeration.
confederation_note: In 1850, the area of today's canton Waadt was a member canton of the Swiss Confederation.

sources.text:
Lausanne ( loh-ZAN, US also  loh-ZAHN; French: [lozan] ) is the capital and largest city of the Swiss French-speaking canton of Vaud, in Switzerland. The Olympic capital, it is a hilly city situated on the shores of Lake Geneva, about halfway between the Jura Mountains and the Alps, and facing the French town of Évian-les-Bains across the lake. Lausanne is 51.7 kilometres (32 miles) northeast of Geneva, the nearest major city. The Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland convenes in Lausanne, although it is not the de jure capital of the nation.
The municipality of Lausanne has a population of about 150,000, making it the fourth largest city in Switzerland after Basel, Geneva, and Zurich, with the entire agglomeration area having about 420,000 inhabitants (as of January 2019).
